review_notes: I read the whole file and checked orderAt and orderAt_apply (@[simp]) in Scheme/Order.lean. I also checked coeff_principalDivisor (@[simp]) in Principal/Basic.lean, and grepped for all uses of ofScheme_ord across the repo. I found no loop risk. orderAt_apply and ofScheme_ord both orient toward X.ord, so they do not compete. The private lemma and the finiteness lemmas are correctly not simp. The only issue I found is the missing composite simp/rw lemma for the repeated three-step unfolding chain. I did not run Lean, so I am not claiming that the proposed lemma compiles or that it makes any particular simp call succeed.

findings.problem: The coefficient of a scheme principal divisor, `coeff ((ofScheme X).principalDivisor g) x`, only reaches its normal form `X.ord ↑(toMul g) x` through three separate rewrites: `coeff_principalDivisor`, then `ofScheme_ord`, then `orderAt_apply`. There is no single canonical lemma for it, even though `ofScheme_ord` is the lemma that finishes the interface. As a result, callers repeat the manual `rw` chain. The same chain, or a prefix of it, appears in ZeroLocus.lean, Sheaf.lean, RiemannRoch/Basic.lean, LocallyPrincipal.lean and Cartier/Basic.lean. Some call sites stop after `ofScheme_ord` and leave `orderAt x g` unfolded, while others add `orderAt_apply`. This makes the normal form inconsistent, and each caller has to remember the exact ordering of rewrites.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `ofScheme_ord`, add a `@[simp]` lemma such as `coeff_principalDivisor_ofScheme (g : Additive X.functionFieldˣ) (x : CodimensionOnePoint X) : WeilDivisor.coeff ((WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.ofScheme X).principalDivisor g) x = X.ord ((Additive.toMul g : X.functionFieldˣ) : X.functionField) x`. Its proof can be `by rw [coeff_principalDivisor, ofScheme_ord, orderAt_apply]`. Then replace the repeated three-step `rw` chains with this one lemma, or with `simp`. The target is the single normal form `X.ord … x`, which is the one already used in the statement of `isEffective_add_principalDivisor_iff`.
findings.benefit: Callers get one stable normal form for coefficients of scheme principal divisors, so they no longer need to re-derive the rewrite order. Proofs such as this one become `rw [coeff_add, coeff_principalDivisor_ofScheme]` or a plain simp call. The lemma is terminating and non-looping: it only unfolds toward `X.ord`, which agrees with the existing `orderAt_apply` direction.

evidence.declaration: coefficient computation for principal divisor of a global section

evidence.excerpt: orderAt x f = X.ord ((Additive.toMul f : X.functionFieldˣ) : X.functionField) x
coeff (S.principalDivisor g) x = S.ord x g
